correctness.rationale: For every coprime a,b>=2, x=bj and y=a(m-j) characterize ALL representations of mab; endpoints cannot be primitive. When m-1 is a prime power, j=1 or m-1 is always primitive. The remaining m=7,11,13,15 have explicit witnesses for every forced allocation of the small prime factors. At m=16, excluding j=1,15 forces primes 3 and 5 to opposite generators, and excluding j=3,9,11 forces 13,7,11 respectively; the converse list of all eight odd-index obstructions and even-index parity is exhaustive. An independently implemented standard-library checker exhaustively covered 729 finite prime states and 13,416 small coprime pairs; no finite extrapolation is used in the proof.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial multiplicative interval of assured primitive representability is a canonical structural invariant for the primitive two-generator Frobenius problem, not a selected arbitrary modulus. Its sharp endpoint at m=16 and complete 55/273 oriented failure locus demonstrate a genuine prime-covering transition and infinitely many naturally defined counterinstances beyond the uniform range, providing concrete guidance for later exact structure questions. This is stronger than a single worked example or a generic CRT lower bound.
